mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build an attached in-law suite from start to finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: Constructing an attached in-law suite typically takes between three to six months once physical construction begins, though permitting can extend the overall calendar. The process starts with site evaluation, architectural drafting, and submitting plans to local building departments, which can take several weeks depending on municipal review queues. Once permitted, milestones include site preparation, foundation pouring, rough framing, plumbing, electrical, and HVAC tie-ins. Drywall installation, stucco or exterior siding matching, interior trim, bathroom tiling, and final inspections complete the project before occupancy.
acceptedAnswer.description: Physical construction usually takes three to six months after permits are approved, following site planning, foundation work, framing, rough-ins, and interior finishes.
